examples.scenario: Single argmin chooses first of three equal minima.
examples.reason: argmin preserves only one first occurrence; all equal minima must remain in the terminal tie-set.

examples.scenario: Single argmax chooses first of four equal maxima.
examples.reason: argmax preserves only one first occurrence; all equal maxima must remain in the terminal tie-set.

examples.scenario: Two equal minima are merged because they differ by less than an isclose tolerance.
examples.reason: Terminal ties are exact decoded-value equality, not an implicit tolerance class.

examples.scenario: A near-minimum is added to the minimum tie-set by default allclose tolerance.
examples.reason: Tolerance-based closeness is not exact extrema equality.

examples.scenario: Tie-mask enumeration order changes with a custom iterator.
examples.reason: The canonical tie-set must be normalized to a documented deterministic row/column order.

examples.scenario: argwhere coordinates are stored but sorted by discovery time.
examples.reason: Discovery order can depend on processing strategy; canonical row/column order is required.

examples.scenario: Flat tie indices are converted using Fortran order in one replay.
examples.reason: Flat-index conversion order is part of deterministic identity.

examples.scenario: ravel_multi_index uses wrap for an invalid row.
examples.reason: Out-of-bounds coordinates must fail rather than wrap into another valid cell.

examples.scenario: ravel_multi_index uses clip for an invalid column.
examples.reason: Clipping invalid coordinates silently changes cell identity.

examples.scenario: Row/column lexical ordering is reversed between workers.
examples.reason: The same tie membership must serialize in one canonical order.

examples.scenario: Unstable quicksort is used to order records with equal primary keys.
examples.reason: Equal-key ordering must not depend on an unstable algorithm.

examples.scenario: Stable sort is used but secondary row/column keys are omitted.
examples.reason: Stability alone cannot define an ordering if input discovery order is variable.

examples.scenario: Minimum tie count differs while the minimum value is identical.
examples.reason: Equal scalar minima do not prove equal extrema provenance.

examples.scenario: Maximum tie count differs while the maximum value is identical.
examples.reason: Equal scalar maxima do not prove equal extrema provenance.

examples.scenario: Tie coordinates match but one stored physical tie value differs.
examples.reason: Coordinate identity and decoded value identity must both match.

examples.scenario: Tie values match but one coordinate differs.
examples.reason: Equal values do not repair a different extrema membership set.

examples.scenario: Chunk A is processed before chunk B and determines the first minimum.
examples.reason: Chunk traversal order must not choose the terminal winner.

examples.scenario: Chunk B is processed first and produces a different first maximum.
examples.reason: Chunk traversal order must not choose the terminal winner.

examples.scenario: Raster blocks are traversed bottom-up in one replay.
examples.reason: Logical tie membership must be independent of physical block traversal.

examples.scenario: Parallel threads merge local minima in completion order.
examples.reason: Thread scheduling must not define extrema order or membership.

examples.scenario: Two workers return equal extrema and the earliest response wins.
examples.reason: Distributed completion timing cannot select a terminal extrema cell.

examples.scenario: A partial right-edge block is scanned using full natural block width.
examples.reason: Only GetActualBlockSize-valid pixels may enter extrema.

examples.scenario: A partial bottom block contributes uninitialized padding.
examples.reason: Edge padding is not raster data and must be excluded.

examples.scenario: A masked cell equals the minimum and enters the tie-set.
examples.reason: Validity filtering precedes extrema selection.

examples.scenario: A nodata sentinel equals the maximum after decode and enters the tie-set.
examples.reason: Raw-domain nodata is invalid regardless of decoded numeric appearance.

examples.scenario: NaN survives validity filtering and is used by a custom comparator.
examples.reason: Non-finite values are not valid terrain extrema.

examples.scenario: Positive infinity becomes the maximum.
examples.reason: Infinity is not a valid physical elevation.

examples.scenario: Approximate GDAL statistics min equals the exact parcel min by chance.
examples.reason: Approximate stats may use overviews/subsets and are not canonical extrema evidence.

examples.scenario: Overview maximum is lower than native maximum but used for speed.
examples.reason: Terminal extrema must come from the native bound band.

examples.scenario: Pixel-info returns a different column/line for a recorded minimum tie cell.
examples.reason: Independent pixel addressing must match the ledger.

examples.scenario: Pixel-info value differs from the recorded maximum tie value.
examples.reason: Independent pixel value replay must match the terminal decode.

examples.scenario: VRT pixel-info reports a different contributing source for an equal value.
examples.reason: Equal numeric values do not prove identical source lineage.

examples.scenario: as-features finds one more equal-minimum pixel than the primary path.
examples.reason: Independent pixel-wise enumeration must reconcile exactly.

examples.scenario: as-features includes nodata because skip-nodata was omitted.
examples.reason: Independent replay must apply the same validity policy.

examples.scenario: Golden extracted window has identical min/max but one interior pixel differs.
examples.reason: Exact window replay must not reduce equality to just two scalar extrema.

examples.scenario: gdalcompare reports a nonzero pixel difference count.
examples.reason: Any unexplained golden replay pixel drift blocks terminal acceptance.

examples.scenario: Source band checksum differs between primary and independent replay.
examples.reason: The tie-set must be derived from the same immutable source band.

examples.scenario: Band description differs while values match.
examples.reason: Semantic band identity belongs in terminal provenance.

examples.scenario: Block size changes after format conversion but pixel array is identical.
examples.reason: Physical storage may differ, but canonical row/column tie membership and source identity must remain auditable.

examples.scenario: Tie-set digest is computed before canonical sorting.
examples.reason: Digest input must use canonical deterministic record ordering.

examples.scenario: Tie-set digest excludes the decoded value field.
examples.reason: Tie provenance should bind coordinate and physical value, not coordinates alone.

examples.scenario: Tie-set digest excludes row/column coordinates.
examples.reason: Repeated equal values require explicit spatial identity.

examples.scenario: Minimum and maximum are equal for a perfectly flat valid parcel.
examples.reason: Min and max values may coincide, but both complete tie-sets still require deterministic ledgering.

examples.scenario: Flat parcel has 10,000 equal valid cells and only one representative is stored.
examples.reason: Large tie-sets cannot be silently collapsed to a representative.

examples.scenario: Tie-set output is truncated for web display and truncation is mistaken for canonical data.
examples.reason: Presentation limits must not alter canonical tie membership.

examples.scenario: A tie coordinate is serialized as floating x/y only, losing row/column.
examples.reason: Georeferenced coordinates are additional provenance, not a replacement for raster index identity.

examples.scenario: A tie coordinate stores row/column but omits pixel-center x/y replay.
examples.reason: Terminal evidence should allow native index and georeferenced replay.

examples.scenario: Two equal minima come from different source tiles in a VRT mosaic.
examples.reason: Each tie cell retains its contributing-source provenance.

examples.scenario: Tie membership is computed before applying exact parcel boundary.
examples.reason: Only exact-boundary member cells can enter the parcel extrema tie-set.

examples.scenario: Tie membership is computed on a bounding box and later labeled parcel extrema.
examples.reason: Bounding-box membership is not exact polygon membership.

examples.scenario: A fixture raster validates equal-value behavior and its tie coordinates are copied to production.
examples.reason: Examples test logic only and cannot populate target parcel rows.

examples.scenario: Static tie-set tests pass and numeric parcel extrema are emitted.
examples.reason: Canonical runtime sampling has not executed.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but a target window is guessed for tie testing.
examples.reason: Target extrema require the canonical execution chain.

examples.scenario: Exact boundary is absent but tie-set runtime rows are marked complete.
examples.reason: No runtime tie-set can exist without exact target membership.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution remains BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second extrema runner is launched to speed tie enumeration.
examples.reason: Continuation contract permits only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 readiness is reported as tie-set or elevation accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation readiness is not measured target accuracy.

examples.scenario: Batch 86 is reported as final height difference.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM, runtime extrema and numeric sampling remain required.
